I am an old woman, I never went to school, but I have been working these fields for thirty years. My husband and I, just the two of us at home now, we manage 14 mu together. I do what my neighbors do, and what worked last year I will do again.

Of my 14 mu, I plant 11 mu in wheat and maize — one after the other, every year, the same as everyone in our village. The other 3 mu I keep in cotton, down by the road. I used to plant more cotton but the price is not good anymore and picking it breaks my back, so I only keep a little for my own money.

For the wheat, after maize comes out in October, my nephew brings the tractor to rotary the ground for me. I sow the improved wheat seed the dealer in town sells — everyone buys it, it comes up well. I put one bag, maybe a bag and a little more, of compound fertilizer (the 15-15-15 kind, 50 jin in a bag) under the seed for each mu. In spring when the wheat turns green I spread half a bag of urea, maybe 20 jin, per mu. If the plants look yellow I add a little more. I water it three times if the well is working — once before winter, once at green-up, once when the heads come out. I spray for aphids and the yellow rust, two times usually, sometimes three if the bugs are bad.

For the maize, soon as the wheat is cut in June I have them no-till sow the hybrid seed right into the stubble — no plowing, that is what everyone does now. I put one bag of compound under it and then 30 jin of urea at knee-high. Water once or twice depending on the rain. Spray once for the borer.

Cotton needs more attention and more spray. I plough that ground because cotton likes loose soil. I use the improved cotton seed, put more fertilizer — maybe a bag and a half of compound plus 30 jin urea at flowering. I spray many times because the bollworm is bad, five or six times through the summer. Water it two or three times.

I would rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than have a thin harvest. Fertilizer money is money, but a bad crop — that is the whole year gone.
